segments.intent: Summarize average body measurements by penguin species
segments.value:
```sql
SELECT
  species,
  COUNT(*) AS penguin_count,
  AVG(bill_length_mm) AS avg_bill_length_mm,
  AVG(bill_depth_mm) AS avg_bill_depth_mm,
  AVG(flipper_length_mm) AS avg_flipper_length_mm,
  AVG(body_mass_g) AS avg_body_mass_g
FROM penguins
GROUP BY species
ORDER BY species
```

<details open><summary>Result</summary>

```
    species penguin_count avg_bill_length_mm avg_bill_depth_mm
1    Adelie           152           38.79139          18.34636
2 Chinstrap            68           48.83382          18.42059

  avg_flipper_length_mm avg_body_mass_g
1              189.9536        3700.662
2              195.8235        3733.088
3              217.1870        5076.016
```

segments.content:
Here are the main differences in average body measurements by species: | Species | Count | Avg bill length (mm) | Avg bill depth (mm) | Avg flipper length (mm) | Avg body mass (g) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Adelie | 152 | 38.79 | 18.35 | 189.95 | 3700.66 | | Chinstrap | 68 | 48.83 | 18.42 | 195.82 | 3733.09 | | Gentoo | 124 | 47.50 | 14.98 | 217.19 | 5076.02 | Key takeaways: - **Adelie** are the **smallest-billed** on average, with the **shortest flippers** and relatively low body mass. - **Chinstrap** have the **longest bills** and the **deepest bills**, but body mass is close to Adelie. - **Gentoo** stand out most: they have **much longer flippers**, are **substantially heavier**, and have the **shallowest bills**. So the clearest species differences are: - **Bill shape:** Chinstrap and Gentoo have longer bills than Adelie, but Gentoo bills are noticeably **less deep**. - **Body size:** Gentoo are much larger overall, especially in **flipper length** and **body mass**. These are species-level averages, so there may still be overlap between individuals.
